segments.text: This trick I'm going to show you is
called the brain scrambler. And it looks
like
this. When you're learning the brain
scrambler, the first thing that you're
going to want to learn is the front
mount. But if you want to work on the
trick without really perfecting the
front mount, there is an easier way to
get the trick started. And that's to
just use your opposite hand to lift the
string right up, just like this, and to
set the yo-yo right on the string. and
that will set you up to do the rest of
the trick. But if you want to get better
at the trick and if you want the trick
to look as good as it possibly can, you
want to learn the front mount. So, I'm
going to show you that first. The first
thing that you're going to want to do is
take your opposite hand and just point
it off to the side. And once you've got
it set there in front of you, you don't
need to move it anymore. It'll make the
trick easier if you just leave it there.
And then what you want to do is get a
good throw. And you kind of want to
swing the yo-yo forward. And on its way
back, it's going to hit that first
finger. and you're going to pull up with
your yo-yo hand, and that'll cause it to
wrap around. And if you're pulling up
straight, then it's going to land right
on the string. And if you've kept this
hand still, then you know that if you're
missing, it's it's your yo-yo hands
fault. So, uh, you may be missing off to
the right or off to the left like that,
but you compensate with your yo-yo hand.
And so, as long as you're pulling it
straight up, you're probably going to
land it right on the string. Once you
get the yo-yo onto the string, then what
you want to do is bring your hands
together and put your yo-yo finger just
below the first finger on your opposite
hand. And you're going to use that
finger to to start the motion off. To
make it just a little bit easier for
yourself, you can swing the yo-yo
forward and that'll give it some
momentum for that first push. And to
complete the trick, all you really need
to do is just one flip. But as you can
see, when I'm doing the trick, you can
do as many flips as you want. And as you
do those flips, the string is going to
wrap around your yo-yo finger. And
that's just
normal. So to dismount the trick, just
like getting it started, how you swing
it forward, you're also going to want to
swing it forward, but this time pull
your opposite finger down. And that'll
cause the yo-yo to swing out and go
forward right in front of you. Just like
that. Now, if you want to add a little
bit of flare to the end of the trick,
you can do a couple of flips, stop it,
give it a little loop at the end, and
that's the brain scrambler.
